THINKING / STRATEGIC DECISION MAP

INDEPENDENT PRACTICE / CAPE TOWN

Are you following a strategy, or just a plan?
← All thinking
View the quadrant map ↓

“Everybody has a plan until they get punched in the mouth.”

— Mike Tyson

A fictional café expands its menu and opening hours. Everyone is busy. Who is it for, and why choose it?

A plan organises work. A strategy chooses who to serve, what to offer and what to leave out.

Let’s map two questions.
Across: are the decisions clear?
The team knows its customers, why they choose it and what it will refuse.
Upwards: does the team follow through?
People know their responsibilities and deliver what they promise.

Clarity of choice

One café. Four possible situations.
Bottom left — Strategic Drift
Commuters, long lunches, evening diners: the café serves everyone. Priorities shift and orders arrive late.
Top left — The Efficient Treadmill
Orders arrive on time, but the broad offer remains. The owner cannot explain why customers should choose this café.
Bottom right — Unrealised Strategy
The owner chooses quick weekday breakfasts for office workers and drops evening service. Slow preparation still leaves customers waiting.
Top right — Coherent Advantage
The breakfast choice shapes the menu, staffing and preparation. Customers are served on time. The owner must still test demand and profitability.

The Efficient Treadmill: delivering a plan well without examining whether its choices make sense.
